items.title: astra-tools
items.text:
astra-tools is the validator, resolver and checker of ASTRA 0.1 analyses. It comes as a command line, astra, and as a Python module, astra.api.

It answers three questions of an analysis, from its files and git alone:

Question Command Function Answer Is it valid? astra validate validate ValidationReport What does it mean? astra info, astra view resolve ResolvedAnalysis How do its results stand? astra status status StatusReport

Each answer is plain data that writes as JSON, and a command's --json prints exactly what the function returns.

astra-tools runs no recipe. A runner, such as lightcone-cli, decides what to build, in what order and where, builds it, and writes each result's record with write_records. The specification says what an analysis means and what each rule asks.

items.title: Install
items.text:
astra-tools needs Python 3.11 or later, and git, which it runs to read repositories.

uv tool install astra-tools   # or: pip install astra-tools
astra --version

While astra-tools for ASTRA 0.1 has only release candidates, uv and pip skip them. Ask for them with uv tool install --prerelease allow astra-tools, or pip install --pre astra-tools.

To run it once without installing it, name the version:

uvx astra-tools@<version> validate

It reads ASTRA 0.1 files, those whose spec_version is 0.1.x. Files written for ASTRA 0.0.x need the 0.2 line of astra-tools (astra-tools<0.3).

items.title: Where to look
items.text: Page What it holds CLI reference Every astra command: its arguments, options, output and exit codes Python API The functions of astra.api, and what they raise Data model Every class the functions return, field by field, and how each writes as JSON

items.title: A first look
items.text:
$ astra init my-analysis
✓ created astra.yaml
✓ created .gitignore
✓ created .git
✓ Converged ASTRA analysis scaffold: my-analysis
$ astra validate my-analysis
astra.yaml: valid, 0 error(s), 0 warning(s)

The same from Python:

from astra import api

report = api.validate("my-analysis")
assert report.valid
analysis = api.resolve("my-analysis")

items.title: Python API
items.text:
astra.api is the whole public surface of astra-tools, and the one module another package imports. Everything else is private and may change.

from astra import api

It holds eight functions, the classes they return (Data model) and the errors they raise (Errors).

Function What it does Returns validate Says whether an analysis is valid ValidationReport resolve Says what an analysis means ResolvedAnalysis status Says how each of its results stands: whether its record still holds StatusReport init_analysis Makes a folder an analysis, where it isn't one nothing write_records Writes a result's record at each of its places nothing paper Looks a paper up in the paper cache Paper, or None add_paper Puts a paper in the paper cache Paper verify_quote Seeks a quote in a cached paper QuoteStatus

The first three are functions of the analysis's files and of git, and nothing else. None runs a recipe. What to build, in what order, where and in which environment is a runner's own business, and nothing here says it.

items.title: Reading an analysis
items.text:
validate, resolve and status read an analysis the same way. path is the analysis's folder, the current folder by default, and it holds the analysis's astra.yaml: nothing is searched for. The analysis is read in the working tree of the git repository that holds it, and each analysis it declares is read with it, in the working tree or at its commit.

A commit of another repository is fetched into the cache, once. With offline=True nothing is fetched, and only the commits kept from earlier fetches can be read.

All three raise:

  • NoAnalysisError where path holds no astra.yaml;
  • GitError where git can't be run;
  • CacheError where the cache can't be used;
  • OSError where a file can't be read.

items.title: validate
items.text:
def validate(path=None, *, offline=False) -> ValidationReport

The validator's report on the analysis: a Diagnostic for each parse, schema and validator rule it breaks, over its whole stack. An analysis that breaks a MUST isn't an error of the function: the report says so, in valid and in its diagnostics.

report = api.validate("my-analysis")
for diagnostic in report.diagnostics:
    at = diagnostic.location
    print(f"{at.file}:{at.line} {diagnostic.level} {diagnostic.code} {diagnostic.message}")

items.title: resolve
items.text:
def resolve(path=None, *, offline=False) -> ResolvedAnalysis

The analysis, resolved: every analysis of its stack with what it declares, each universe's selection, and its results, each with its places, what it reads and its command as it runs. It also gives head, the commit the repository is on. Every rule of the specification is already applied, so a reader follows ids and applies none itself.

Raises InvalidAnalysisError where the analysis breaks a MUST: only a valid analysis resolves. The error's report is the validator's report.

analysis = api.resolve("my-analysis")
for result in analysis.results:
    print(result.id, result.places[0].file_path, result.command)

items.title: status
items.text:
def status(path=None, *, offline=False) -> StatusReport

How the analysis's results stand: for each result that resolve gives, its Status, under the result's id; and the status of each evidence that cites an output. The records and bytes are the ones in the working tree.

A result's status says whether its record still holds: whether anything the result is made from has changed since the commit the record names. This is what the specification calls checking, and its check rules are the ones a status reports.

The report also says where the bytes of each result and of each input are, and which large-file tool keeps them. A result's state doesn't depend on its bytes: a clone that hasn't fetched them reads as up to date. astra-tools never fetches, so a runner reads what needs it:

for ref, content in report.inputs.items():
    if content.state == "absent":
        print(f"{ref} needs fetching with {content.kept_by}")

git-annex and Git LFS are read without their content. An input kept by DVC must be pulled for the results made from it to be compared (why).

The report holds none of the analysis: resolve gives that. Raises InvalidAnalysisError where the analysis breaks a MUST.

report = api.status("my-analysis")
for id, status in report.statuses.items():
    print(id, status.state, status.bytes, [broken.code for broken in status.why])

items.title: Asking for both
items.text:
A runner needs both what the results are and how each stands, so it calls resolve and status. Each reads the working tree, and each gives head, the commit the repository was on. Where the two differ, something was committed between the calls, and the runner asks again:

analysis = api.resolve(folder)
report = api.status(folder)
if report.head != analysis.head:
    raise RuntimeError("the repository moved between the two readings: ask again")

head names the commit, not the files. A runner builds only from a committed tree, so for it the same head is the same files. Where the working tree has uncommitted changes, two readings at the same head can still differ.

items.title: init_analysis
items.text:
def init_analysis(directory) -> None

Converges directory into an analysis. Where it has no astra.yaml, one is written with a spec_version and a label, and nothing declared. The folder is made if need be.

It is idempotent: an astra.yaml already there is left exactly as it is. A second call changes nothing, and a folder that already holds an analysis is safe to pass.

Nothing else is written or looked at, so a tool scaffolds into a folder under its own conventions. astra init calls it, and adds a .gitignore and a git repository.

Raises OSError where the file can't be written.

items.title: write_records
items.text:
def write_records(folder, result, content_hash, size, generated_by) -> None

Records a result as a run made it. folder is the analysis's folder, result a Result of its resolved analysis, content_hash and size the hash (sha256:<hex>) and size of the bytes the recipe made, and generated_by the run, a Generation.

A ProvenanceRecord is written at each of the result's places, with that place's address. Each is JSON with sorted keys, written to a temporary file and moved into place.

What a record says is the runner's to find out, and true of its run: this function hashes no file and reads no checkout.

Raises ValueError, and writes nothing, where:

  • result is a result from a commit (it has a commit): it is never built, and its places aren't in the working tree;
  • the record would be invalid: generated_by hasn't one item of inputs for each entry the result's output lists, or a field hasn't the form the record schema asks for.

Raises OSError where a record can't be written.

items.title: Papers
items.text:
The paper functions are apart from the rest. They aren't functions of an analysis's files: the paper cache is a folder of this machine, add_paper uses the network, and matching a quote against a PDF's text is astra-tools' own, as the specification has no rule on it.

A paper is kept under its DOI as it was given and, where one was given, its version. The lookup is exact: version=7 and no version are two papers.

All three raise CacheError where the cache can't be used.

items.title: paper
items.text:
def paper(doi, *, version=None) -> Paper | None

The paper of doi in the paper cache, at version where evidence gives one; None where it isn't there.

items.title: add_paper
items.text:
def add_paper(doi, *, version=None, pdf=None) -> Paper

Puts the paper of doi in the cache, and returns it. With pdf, the PDF at that path is kept. With none, an arXiv DOI (10.48550/arXiv.<id>) is downloaded from arXiv, at version where one is given; no other paper is downloaded. A paper already in the cache is returned as it is.

Raises PaperError where no PDF can be got or the file isn't a PDF, and OSError where pdf can't be read.

items.title: verify_quote
items.text:
def verify_quote(doi, quote, *, version=None, location=None) -> QuoteStatus

Whether quote, a TextQuoteSelector, is in the cached paper of doi. With location, a FragmentSelector that gives a page of a PDF (page=6), the quote is to be on that page. The arguments are the fields of an Evidence, so one from a resolved analysis passes straight in:

for each in analysis.analyses:
    for insight in each.prior_insights:
        for evidence in insight.evidence:
            if evidence.doi and evidence.quote:
                status = api.verify_quote(
                    evidence.doi,
                    evidence.quote,
                    version=evidence.version,
                    location=evidence.location,
                )
                print(insight.ref, status.state, status.page)

The match allows for what extracting a PDF's text changes, and a quote's prefix or suffix tells one passage from another like it. A paper that isn't in the cache is a state of the status, no_paper, not an error.

Raises PaperError where the PDF's text can't be read.

items.title: Errors
items.text: Error Raised where NoAnalysisError A folder holds no astra.yaml InvalidAnalysisError The analysis breaks a MUST, so it has no resolved analysis and no statuses. Its report attribute is the ValidationReport GitError git can't be run CacheError The cache can't be used where the environment puts it PaperError A paper can't be put in the cache, or its PDF's text can't be read

items.title: A runner, in brief
items.text:
This is the least a runner does with the API: ask for the analysis and for the status of its results, build what isn't unchanged in the order the results come in, and record each. It leaves out what the specification's runner rules ask for, such as building only from a committed tree.

import hashlib
import subprocess
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

from astra import api


def digest(path: Path) -> tuple[str, int]:
    data = path.read_bytes()
    return f"sha256:{hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}", len(data)


def now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="milliseconds").replace("+00:00", "Z")


folder = Path(".")
analysis = api.resolve(folder)
report = api.status(folder)
if analysis.head is None or report.head != analysis.head:
    raise SystemExit("the repository has no commit, or moved between the two readings")
analyses = {each.key: each for each in analysis.analyses}
inputs = {each.ref: each for one in analysis.analyses for each in one.inputs}
results = {each.id: each for each in analysis.results}

for result in analysis.results:  # each comes after every result it reads
    if report.statuses[result.id].state == "unchanged" or result.command is None:
        continue  # up to date, or not built from the working tree alone
    # What each entry reads: an input's file, or another result's bytes.
    read = []
    for source in result.inputs:
        if source.input is not None:
            path = inputs[source.input].path
        else:
            path = results[source.result].places[0].file_path
        read.append(api.RecordedInput(source.entry, *digest(folder / path)))
    # The recipe runs in the folder of the analysis its output belongs to.
    owner = analyses[".".join(result.output.split(".")[:-2])]
    started = now()
    subprocess.run(result.command, shell=True, cwd=folder / owner.folder, check=True)
    generation = api.Generation(
        commit=analysis.head,
        environment=api.Environment("urn:example:python-3.13"),
        runner=api.Runner("example-runner", "0.1.0"),
        inputs=tuple(read),
        started=started,
        finished=now(),
    )
    api.write_records(folder, result, *digest(folder / result.places[0].file_path), generation)

After it, astra status reads the record back:

$ astra status
fit#baseline  unchanged  present  .astra/records/baseline/fit.json
  made in urn:example:python-3.13 by example-runner 0.1.0
1 result(s), 1 unchanged, 0 stale, 0 missing; 0 absent

items.title: CLI reference
items.text: astra validates ASTRA analyses, shows what they mean, and checks what was built against its records. It runs no recipe: a runner builds the results and writes their records, and astra reads them.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• PATH is an analysis's folder, the current folder by default. Nothing is searched for: the analysis is the astra.yaml in that folder. astra validate and astra info name the analysis another way, each described below.
  • A valid analysis. info, view, status and history answer only for an analysis that breaks no MUST. For one that does, they print what astra validate prints, and exit 1.
  • Exit codes:
    • 0 when the command answers;
    • 1 when the analysis breaks a MUST, a result isn't unchanged, or what was asked for isn't there (no analysis, nothing in git, a paper or a quote);
    • 2 for a usage error, an analysis that can't be read, a broken environment (git or the cache unusable, a folder that can't be written), or an internal error.
  • Diagnostics are grouped by file, one per line, as line:col level CODE message. A code is a rule of the specification, listed under Rules, or one of astra-tools' own. The level is error for a MUST broken and warning for a SHOULD.
  • JSON. validate, info and status take --json, and print the data model as it writes: validate a ValidationReport, info a ResolvedAnalysis, and status a StatusReport. The paper commands that verify quotes print QuoteStatus. The exit code is the same with and without --json.
  • Colour is left out where NO_COLOR is set, or where the output isn't a terminal.
  • The cache keeps the commits fetched from remotes, the validity of analyses read at a commit, the hashes of files, and papers. It sits outside every repository: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/astra or ~/.cache/astra on Linux, ~/Library/Caches/astra on macOS. ASTRA_CACHE_DIR, an absolute path, moves it.
  • astra --help, and --help after any command, give each command's options. astra --version gives astra-tools' version. ASTRA_DEBUG=1 prints the traceback of an internal error.

The examples come from one small analysis:

spec_version: "0.1.0"
label: Example
inputs:
  catalog: {path: data/catalog.csv}
decisions:
  method:
    options: {ols: {}, robust: {}}
outputs:
  fit:
    type: metric
    format: json
    inputs: [catalog]
    decisions: [method]
    recipe:
      command: python fit.py {inputs.catalog} {decisions.method} {output}
universes:
  baseline:
    decisions: {method: ols}

items.title: Commands at a glance
items.text: Command What it does astra init Make a minimal analysis, or complete one astra validate Validate an analysis and its whole stack astra info Show an analysis in brief astra view Show the analysis as it is in one universe astra status Show how each result stands: its record and its bytes astra history Show what git holds of a result's records over time astra spec Describe the fields of ASTRA files astra schema Show or export the LinkML schemas astra guide Print the guide for agents astra paper Keep cited papers, and verify quotes in them

items.title: astra init
items.text:
astra init [DIRECTORY] [--check] [--json]

Converges DIRECTORY, the current folder by default, into a minimal analysis. It creates whatever is missing and never writes over a file: an astra.yaml with a spec_version and a label, a .gitignore, and a git repository where none holds DIRECTORY already. A folder that has an astra.yaml or other files is adopted, not refused, so it is safe to run again.

Option Meaning --check Write nothing: report what would be created, and exit 1 where something would --json Print the report as JSON: converged, and the names created, repaired, unchanged, and warnings 
$ astra init my-analysis
✓ created astra.yaml
✓ created .gitignore
✓ created .git
✓ Converged ASTRA analysis scaffold: my-analysis
$ cat my-analysis/astra.yaml
# ASTRA Analysis Specification

spec_version: "0.1.0"
label: "my-analysis"

items.title: astra validate
items.text:
astra validate [FILE] [-e | --verify-evidence] [--skip-evidence] [--json] [--offline]

Checks every parse, schema and validator rule over the whole stack: the analysis and every analysis it declares, each at its commit. It reads no results; astra status does. Exits 0 when every analysis is valid and 1 when one breaks a MUST. A SHOULD that is broken is a warning, and doesn't change the exit code.

FILE is an analysis's astra.yaml, or its folder. With no FILE, every root analysis under the current folder is validated: each astra.yaml that no other one declares. Hidden folders, node_modules, venv, __pycache__ and results aren't searched.

Option Meaning -e, --verify-evidence Also seek each quote of the analysis's evidence in the paper it cites, which must be in the paper cache (astra paper add) --skip-evidence Verify no evidence, and don't suggest it --json Print the ValidationReport as JSON: for FILE, the one report; with no FILE, a list of them, one for each root analysis --offline Fetch nothing: use only the commits fetched before

An analysis declared by url and commit is fetched into the cache, once.

Here the universe baseline has been edited to select lasso:

$ astra validate
astra.yaml
  18:25 error UNKNOWN_OPTION `method` has no option `lasso`: its options are `ols`, `robust`
astra.yaml: invalid, 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

1/1 file(s) failed validation: astra.yaml
$ astra validate astra.yaml --json
{
  "root": "astra.yaml",
  "valid": false,
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "code": "UNKNOWN_OPTION",
      "level": "error",
      "message": "`method` has no option `lasso`: its options are `ols`, `robust`",
      "location": {
        "file": "astra.yaml",
        "pointer": "/universes/baseline/decisions/method",
        "line": 18,
        "column": 25
      },
      "related": []
    }
  ],
  "unchecked": []
}

With --verify-evidence, a quote that isn't verified is an error of the report, at its place in astra.yaml, under one of three codes of astra-tools' own:

Code Meaning EVIDENCE_PAPER_MISSING The paper the evidence cites isn't in the paper cache EVIDENCE_PAPER_UNREADABLE The paper is in the cache, and its text can't be read EVIDENCE_QUOTE_NOT_FOUND The quote isn't in the paper, or isn't on the page its location gives (page=6)

Each quote is sought as astra paper verify-quote and api.verify_quote seek one: it is the same check. Evidence that cites an output has no paper to seek a quote in, and evidence with no quote nothing to seek: each is counted as skipped, and neither fails.

items.title: astra info
items.text:
astra info [-f FILE | --file FILE] [-d] [-i] [-o] [--json]

Shows the analysis in brief: its label and description, how many inputs, outputs, decisions, universes and planned results it has, then its inputs, outputs, decisions and universes, each universe with the option it selects for each decision it uses. Each other analysis of the stack follows, the same way, under its key and its file.

The analysis is the astra.yaml in the current folder or the nearest folder above it that has one; --file names it instead, by its astra.yaml or its folder. Exits 1 where there is no analysis, or it breaks a MUST.

Option Meaning -f, --file FILE The analysis's astra.yaml, or its folder -d, --decisions Show only the decisions -i, --inputs Show only the inputs -o, --outputs Show only the outputs --json Print the ResolvedAnalysis as JSON

-d, -i and -o combine: -d -i shows the decisions and the inputs.

$ astra info
Example
Spec version: 0.1.0

Inputs: 1 | Outputs: 1 | Decisions: 1 | Universes: 1
Planned results: 1

Inputs:
┏━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ ID      ┃ Path             ┃ Description ┃
┡━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ catalog │ data/catalog.csv │             │
└─────────┴──────────────────┴─────────────┘

Outputs:
┏━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ ID  ┃ Type   ┃ Format ┃ Description ┃
┡━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ fit │ metric │ json   │             │
└─────┴────────┴────────┴─────────────┘

Decisions:
method:
└── Options:
    ├── ols:
    └── robust:


Universes:
  baseline: decisions.method = ols

items.title: astra view
items.text:
astra view UNIVERSE [PATH]

Shows the analysis as it is in UNIVERSE, one of its universes: the option the universe selects for each decision it uses, then each result planned in it, with its id, where its bytes go, what each entry of its output's inputs reads there, through any switch, and its command as it runs. Exits 2 where the analysis has no universe UNIVERSE.

$ astra view baseline
universe baseline
  decisions.method = ols
fit#baseline  results/baseline/fit.json
  catalog reads inputs.catalog
  $ python fit.py data/catalog.csv ols results/baseline/fit.json

items.title: astra status
items.text:
astra status [PATH] [--json]

Shows how each result of the analysis stands, by the specification's check rules, with the records and bytes that are in the working tree. For each result it checks the record and the bytes:

  • the record is unchanged, stale (something the result is made from has changed since the commit the record names) or missing;
  • the bytes are present (the ones the record gives, at the result's place) or absent.

Each result is shown with its state, its bytes' and where its record goes, and under it each rule it breaks. Then each evidence that cites an output gets the status of what it cites. Exits 0 when every result and evidence is unchanged, and 1 otherwise.

Option Meaning --json Print the StatusReport as JSON: the commit the repository is on, each result's status by its id, and the evidence's 
$ astra status
fit#baseline  missing  absent  .astra/records/baseline/fit.json
  error MISSING_RECORD no record is at .astra/records/baseline/fit.json: build `fit#baseline`, and record it there
1 result(s), 0 unchanged, 0 stale, 1 missing; 1 absent

Each result's bytes, and each input's, come with the tool that keeps them where a stand-in is at the file's path: absent, kept by git-annex says the content isn't in this clone, and which tool fetches it. An input whose content isn't here is listed after the results. astra fetches nothing. A result reads the same whether or not its own bytes are fetched.

An input is another matter, as a result is made from it. git-annex links, with keys of a SHA-256 backend, and Git LFS pointers are compared by the hash they give, so such an input needn't be fetched. A DVC file gives no SHA-256: an input kept by DVC must be pulled, or the results made from it read stale and the command exits 1 (Data model).

A link is followed only for a stand-in: a git-annex link to the file it leads to in an annex/objects folder, and what is at the path beside a DVC file (Data model).

items.title: astra history
items.text:
astra history timeline ADDR [PATH]
astra history lineage ADDR [PATH] [--used-by]
astra history find (--hash H | --environment IRI) [PATH]
astra history get ADDR@REV [PATH]

Reads a result's records over time, from git. ADDR is a result's address, as its record gives it (fit#baseline, summary); astra status lists them. A record's versions are its file at each commit along HEAD's history that changed it, in the repository that holds the analysis the result belongs to. Exits 1 where what is asked for isn't in git, and 2 where ADDR names no planned result or REV names no commit.

Command What it shows timeline ADDR Each version of the result's record, newest first: the commit that changed it, and the hash, size, commit, end and environment it gives lineage ADDR What the result was made from, as its record at HEAD gives it, down to the input files. With --used-by, the planned results whose records at HEAD list it instead find The versions of planned results' records whose bytes have the hash --hash gives (sha256:<hex>), or whose environment is the IRI --environment gives get ADDR@REV The bytes the result had at the commit REV names (a commit, a branch, a tag), checked against its record there, written to standard output

items.title: astra spec
items.text:
astra spec [TERM] [--full]

Describes the fields of ASTRA files, from the specification's LinkML schema. Without TERM, it prints a summary of the concepts. With TERM, in any case, it prints that entry. --full prints every entry, which is long.

items.title: astra schema
items.text:
astra schema show (analysis | insights | provenance | types)
astra schema export [-o DIR | --output DIR]

The LinkML schemas of ASTRA files, as astra-spec ships them. show prints one to standard output. export writes them all into DIR, schemas/ by default.

items.title: astra guide
items.text:
astra guide

Prints astra-spec's guide for agents, llms.txt, unchanged.

items.title: astra paper
items.text:
astra paper add DOI [-v N | --version N] [--pdf FILE]
astra paper list
astra paper show DOI [-v N]
astra paper path DOI [-v N]
astra paper remove DOI [-v N]
astra paper fetch-metadata [DOI] [-v N] [--all]
astra paper verify-quote DOI (-q TEXT | --quote TEXT) [-v N] [-p N | --page N] [--json]
astra paper verify-quotes DOI [-v N]

Keeps the papers that evidence cites by DOI in the paper cache, and seeks quotes in them. A paper is kept under its DOI as given, and its version where one is given: -v 7 and no version are two papers.

Command What it does add DOI Keeps the paper of DOI. An arXiv DOI (10.48550/arXiv.<id>) is downloaded from arXiv, at --version where given. No other paper is downloaded: --pdf keeps a PDF you have. A paper already kept is left as it is. Exits 1 where the paper can't be got list Lists the papers in the cache show DOI Shows a paper's title, authors, hash, source and path. Exits 1 where it isn't in the cache path DOI Prints the path of the paper's PDF, and nothing else. Exits 1 where it isn't in the cache remove DOI Removes the paper from the cache. Exits 1 where it isn't there fetch-metadata [DOI] Fetches the title and authors of a kept paper from doi.org; with --all, of every kept paper that lacks them verify-quote DOI Seeks one quote in the paper verify-quotes DOI Seeks several quotes in the paper, read from standard input

items.title: Verifying quotes
items.text:
A quote is sought in the text of the paper's PDF. The match allows for what extracting a PDF's text changes: line breaks, ligatures, a character read wrong. Each quote gets a QuoteStatus:

state Meaning found The quote is in the paper, on page elsewhere The quote is in the paper on page, and not on the page it was said to be on not_found The quote isn't in the paper no_paper The paper isn't in the cache

Both commands exit 0 when every quote is found, 1 otherwise, and 2 where the paper's text can't be read.

verify-quote takes the quote as --quote, and with --page the page it is to be on. --json prints its status.

$ astra paper add 10.9999/example --pdf paper.pdf
$ astra paper verify-quote 10.9999/example -q "reduce the influence of outliers" -p 2
✓ Found on page 2
$ astra paper verify-quote 10.9999/example -q "reduce the influence of outliers" -p 1 --json
{
  "state": "elsewhere",
  "page": 2
}

verify-quotes reads a JSON list from standard input, an item for each quote. An item has the quote of an evidence item and, where it has one, its location, as astra.yaml writes them:

[
  {"quote": {"exact": "reduce the influence of outliers"}, "location": {"value": "page=2"}},
  {"quote": {"exact": "a sentence the paper never says anywhere", "prefix": "and then "}}
]

It prints a JSON list of each quote's status, in the same order:

[
  {
    "state": "found",
    "page": 2
  },
  {
    "state": "not_found"
  }
]

It exits 2, and prints nothing, where the input isn't such a list.

items.title: Data model
items.text:
The data model is what the functions of astra.api return, and what a runner hands back. It is defined in src/astra/model/, a file for each thing a function returns, and those files hold nothing else.

File Classes Where they come from validation_report.py ValidationReport validate returns it resolved_analysis.py ResolvedAnalysis and the classes it is made of resolve returns it status_report.py StatusReport, Status, EvidenceStatus status returns it provenance_record.py ProvenanceRecord, Generation and its parts a runner gives write_records a Generation; a Status holds the record diagnostic.py Diagnostic, Location the reports hold them paper.py Paper, QuoteStatus the paper functions return them

Every class is imported from astra.api.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• Plain data. Every class is a frozen dataclass that holds what JSON holds: text, numbers, true and false, lists and maps. In Python a list is a tuple, and a map a read-only mapping.
  • A reference is an id, never an object. Where one element names another, it holds the other's id as text, and a reader looks it up.
  • Each fact once. What a reader gets by following a reference isn't repeated.
  • One JSON form. Each class writes as a JSON object that holds every field under its name. An optional field is left out where it has no value, and is never null. A list or a map is always there, empty or not. ValidationReport, ResolvedAnalysis and StatusReport have a to_json() method that gives it.

In the tables below, optional marks a field that can have no value.

items.title: JSON report contract
items.text:
Each report carries a fixed schema_version: astra-tools.validation-report.v1, astra-tools.resolved-analysis.v1 or astra-tools.status-report.v1. This identifies the JSON format, independently of the authored ASTRA spec_version and the astra-tools package version. The field is set by the report class and adds no constructor argument.

The packaged reports.schema.json is a JSON Schema 2019-09 document. Its $defs contain the three report types and their nested types; the document itself accepts any of the three reports. Other languages can consume it without Python. It checks transport structure, not reference integrity or the rules applied by validate, resolve and status. In Python, read it with:

from importlib.resources import files

schema_json = files("astra.model").joinpath("reports.schema.json").read_text("utf-8")

Within a format version, producers may add optional fields; readers should ignore unknown fields. Removing or renaming a field, changing its type or meaning, adding a required field, or making an optional field required needs a new format version. Lists keep the ordering described below; JSON object member order is not part of the interchange contract. Optional fields remain omitted, never null.

Generate the schema from the Python model with uv run --frozen python scripts/generate-report-schema.py; tests check it for drift. Small, reproducible report fixtures provide expected JSON for independent implementations; they supplement the specification's validation conformance suite.

The diagrams are UML class diagrams. A filled diamond is on a class that holds another; a hollow diamond is on a class that refers to another by its ref or id. The number beside a class says how many, and [0..1] after a field marks an optional one, [*] a list.

{"root": "astra.yaml", "valid": true, "diagnostics": [], "unchecked": [], "schema_version": "astra-tools.validation-report.v1"}

items.title: The resolved analysis
items.text:
A resolved analysis is an analysis with every rule of the specification already applied. Two rules decide what is in it.

It holds what the rules give, not what they start from. Where an astra.yaml writes something only for a rule to act on, the model holds the outcome: a universe's effective selection and no derived_from, what each entry of an output's inputs reads and no switch, a command as it runs and no template. What a file writes for people to read stays as written: labels, descriptions, rationales, claims, quotes.

It holds each fact once. A result carries its places, what it reads and its command. It carries neither the options it is made with (its output's decisions, looked up in its universe's selection) nor the folder its recipe runs in (its output's analysis's folder).

items.title: References, ids and paths
items.text:
• A ref names an element among all the analyses of the stack: its analysis's key, the collection the file writes it in, and its id, joined by dots. outputs.fit is an output of the driving analysis, and stage.decisions.method a decision of the analysis stage.
  • An analysis's key is its canonical address: the shortest chain of declarations that reaches it from the driving analysis, the first in alphabetical order among equals, and "" for the driving analysis itself.
  • A result's id is its address, as its record gives it (fit#baseline), after the key of the analysis it belongs to and a colon where that isn't the driving analysis (stage:fit#v1).
  • Every path is a path from the driving analysis's folder, with / between folders and . for that folder itself. A file of an analysis read at a commit is in that commit's tree, from the top of the repository it is read in. A diagnostic's location isn't such a path: it names its file from the top of the repository.

items.title: ResolvedAnalysis
items.text:
Field Type Meaning spec_version str The driving analysis's spec_version head str, optional The commit the repository is on, as HEAD names it; none where it has no commit yet analyses list of Analysis The driving analysis, then each it declares, directly or not, by key results list of Result The results, each after every result it reads notes list of Diagnostic What an author may want to tidy, which breaks no rule schema_version str Always astra-tools.resolved-analysis.v1; the JSON report format

The notes are FALLBACK_PIN, UNPLANNED_OUTPUT and NOT_BUILT, at the level note, and the runner rule CODE_OUTSIDE_ANALYSIS, a warning.

head names the commit, not the files: the analysis is read in the working tree, so where a file is edited and not committed, two readings at the same head can differ. A StatusReport has the same field, so a reader that asked for both can tell that nothing was committed between the two.

items.text:
What an analysis declares it makes. A switch isn't one: where a file writes a switch, each result that reads it names what it reads there, in its inputs.

Field Type Meaning ref str type str metric, figure, table, data or report format str The file format, such as json label str, optional description str, optional tags list of str resources Resources, optional What its recipe asks for decisions list of str The decisions it is made with, by ref

items.text:
A claim backed by evidence: what an analysis builds on, or what it concludes.

Field Type Meaning ref str kind str prior_insight or finding claim str evidence list of Evidence label str, optional description str, optional scope str, optional tags list of str

items.title: Evidence
items.text:
What a claim rests on: a work, by its doi, or the results of an output, in cites.

Field Type Meaning doi str, optional The work's DOI version int, optional The work's version cites list of str, optional For evidence that cites an output, the id of each result it cites; empty where the output has no result quote TextQuoteSelector, optional location FragmentSelector, optional artifact str, optional The artifact address as authored, scoped to the analysis containing the insight

artifact preserves a switch address and any #universe pin. It remains present when cites is empty, so a reader can identify what the author cited even where no result is planned. It is an authored address, not a canonical ref. Evidence citing a DOI has no artifact.

items.title: TextQuoteSelector
items.text:
A passage quoted exactly.

Field Type Meaning exact str The passage prefix str, optional The text just before it suffix str, optional The text just after it

items.title: FragmentSelector
items.text:
A place in a work or an output, as a fragment identifier.

Field Type Meaning value str The fragment identifier, such as page=6 conforms_to str, optional The syntax it follows, as an IRI

items.title: Universe
items.text:
A universe of an analysis, with the option it selects for each decision it uses.

Field Type Meaning ref str selection map of str to str A decision's ref, and the id of the option selected: exactly the decisions the universe uses label str, optional description str, optional tags list of str

items.title: Result
items.text:
A result: one output, in one universe or once.

The results are those of the outputs the driving analysis builds, each in every universe that builds it, and the results those read, in whatever analysis they belong to. The specification says the analysis plans these. An output with no result, such as one of a declared analysis that nothing reads, is named in the notes.

Field Type Meaning id str output str Its output, by ref places list of Place Where it is kept: one place, unless its analysis is driven through two chains of declarations universe str, optional Its universe, by ref; none for an output built once inputs list of Source One for each entry of its output's inputs, in order command str, optional Its recipe's command as it runs, in the folder of its output's analysis, with each path relative to that folder commit Commit, optional The commit whose tree its places are in, where the analysis it belongs to is read at one; none for a result whose places are in the working tree

A result has no command where it isn't built from the working tree alone: a result of an analysis read at a commit, one whose recipe runs on a commit's files, or one that reads a file at a commit.

A result with a commit is a result from a commit: it is never built, its record is the one at that commit, and write_records refuses it.

items.title: Place
items.text:
Where one name of a result is kept.

Field Type Meaning address str The name, then # and the universe's id for a result built in one record_path str Where its record goes file_path str The result's file, where its bytes go. A stand-in may be there in their place: its Status says

items.title: Source
items.text:
What one entry of an output's inputs reads for a result: an input, or another result, through any pin and the case each switch on the way takes. It has input or result, never both.

Field Type Meaning entry str The entry, as the output's inputs writes it input str, optional The input it reads, by ref result str, optional The result it reads, by id

items.title: The status report
items.text:
A status report says how the results of an analysis stand: one status for each result of the resolved analysis, with the records and bytes that are in the working tree. It holds none of the analysis itself. Each status is under its result's id, and resolve gives the result.

A result is unchanged where it has a record at each of its places and nothing it is made from has changed since the commit the record names; stale where something has; and missing where a place has no record that is the result's own.

Separately, the report says where the bytes of each result and of each input are: present where reading the file gives its content, and absent otherwise. A result's state doesn't depend on its bytes, so a clone that hasn't fetched what a large-file tool keeps reads as up to date, with those bytes absent.

classDiagram
  direction LR
  class StatusReport {
    head : str [0..1]
  }
  class Status {
    state : unchanged, stale or missing
    stale_inputs : entry [*]
  }
  class Bytes {
    state : present or absent
    kept_by : str [0..1]
  }
  class EvidenceStatus {
    insight : ref
    index : int
    state : unchanged, stale or missing
  }
  class ProvenanceRecord
  class Result
  class Input
  class Diagnostic
  class Insight
  StatusReport *-- "*" Status : statuses, by result id
  StatusReport *-- "*" EvidenceStatus : evidence
  StatusReport *-- "*" Bytes : inputs, by input ref
  StatusReport o-- "*" Result : statuses, by id
  StatusReport o-- "*" Input : inputs, by ref
  Status *-- "0..1" Bytes : bytes
  Status *-- "0..1" ProvenanceRecord : record
  Status *-- "*" Diagnostic : why
  EvidenceStatus *-- "*" Diagnostic : why
  EvidenceStatus o-- "1" Insight : insight

items.title: StatusReport
items.text: Field Type Meaning head str, optional The commit the repository was on when it was read, as ResolvedAnalysis gives it statuses map of str to Status Each result's status, by the result's id, in the results' order evidence list of EvidenceStatus The status of each evidence that cites an output inputs map of str to Bytes Where each input's content is, by the input's ref schema_version str Always astra-tools.status-report.v1; the JSON report format

items.title: Status
items.text:
A result's status: the worst of its places'.

Field Type Meaning state str unchanged, stale or missing bytes Bytes, optional Where its bytes are; none for a result of an analysis read at a commit that no recipe reads record ProvenanceRecord, optional Its record, where every place holds one that is the result's: the first place's why list of Diagnostic Each rule the result itself breaks stale_inputs list of str Each entry of its output's inputs that reads a result that isn't unchanged, or one made again since with other bytes than the record gives

A result that is stale with no error in why is stale only through what it reads. It is unchanged again once each of those is built with the bytes its record gives for the entry, which a runner that builds them can tell without a second check.

items.title: Bytes
items.text:
Whether the content of a file the analysis names is in this clone: an input's, or a result's.

Field Type Meaning state str present where reading the file's path gives the content; absent otherwise. For a result, the content is the one its record gives kept_by str, optional The tool whose stand-in is at the path: git-annex, Git LFS or DVC

absent with a kept_by means the content needs fetching, with that tool. astra-tools never fetches: when and how is a runner's to decide.

A stand-in is what a large-file tool keeps in a file's place. astra-tools reads three:

Tool Its stand-in The content is here when Compared without the content git-annex, locked file A link at the path, into an annex/objects folder The link leads to a file Yes, for a key of a SHA-256 backend, which is the default git-annex, unlocked file A pointer file at the path, only while the content isn't fetched The path holds the content Yes, the same Git LFS A pointer file at the path, only while the content isn't fetched The path holds the content Yes DVC A .dvc file beside the path A file is at the path, or a link from DVC's cache No: it gives an MD5, and a record a SHA-256

So with git-annex and Git LFS, an analysis whose inputs and results aren't fetched validates, and its results read unchanged. With DVC, results that aren't fetched read unchanged too, but an input kept by DVC must be pulled for the results made from it to be compared: until then they read stale. The same holds for a git-annex key of a backend other than SHA-256.

astra-tools follows a link only for a stand-in, as the operating system follows it:

  • a git-annex link, to the file it leads to, where that file really is in an annex/objects folder. So a submodule or a linked worktree works, whose object store is outside its tree, and a link merely dressed as git-annex's leads nowhere;
  • what is at the path beside a DVC file, wherever it leads, as DVC's cache can be anywhere.

A link that is no stand-in's is never followed. This favours convenience: a repository can make astra status say whether a file is at a path of your machine, and whether it has a hash the repository gives, by a link beside a .dvc file. It never shows a file's content. That matters only where you run astra on a repository you don't trust and show its output.

kept_by names the stand-in that is on disk. A file whose content a tool has put in place of its pointer, as git-annex does for an unlocked file and Git LFS always, reads as a plain file.

ABSENT_RESULT, a warning, is for bytes that are neither at a result's file nor stood in for there: no file, other bytes, or a stand-in for other bytes. A stand-in for the recorded bytes breaks no rule.

items.title: EvidenceStatus
items.text:
An item of evidence that cites an output, and the status it gets: the worst of the results it cites, and missing where it cites none.

Field Type Meaning insight str The insight it backs, by ref index int Which item of the insight's evidence, from zero state str unchanged, stale or missing why list of Diagnostic STALE_EVIDENCE, where it isn't unchanged

  "schema_version": "astra-tools.status-report.v1"
}

items.title: The provenance record
items.text:
A record is a runner's account of how it made a result, kept at the result's place. What it says is the runner's to find out, and true of its run. The classes have the fields of the specification's record schema.

    address : str
    content_hash : str
    size : int
    spec_version : str
  }
  class Generation {
    commit : str
    started : str [0..1]
    finished : str [0..1]
  }
  class RecordedInput {
    entry : str
    content_hash : str
    size : int
  }
  class Environment {
    iri : str
  }
  class Runner {
    id : str
    version : str
  }

  Generation *-- "1" Environment : environment
  Generation *-- "1" Runner : runner
  Generation *-- "*" RecordedInput : inputs

items.title: ProvenanceRecord
items.text: Field Type Meaning address str The result's address at this place content_hash str The hash of the result's bytes, as sha256:<hex> size int Their size, in bytes generated_by Generation The run that made it spec_version str The version of the specification the record is written for

items.title: Generation
items.text:
A run of an output's recipe.

Field Type Meaning commit str The commit it ran from environment Environment The environment it ran in runner Runner The runner that ran it inputs list of RecordedInput What it read: one for each entry the output's inputs lists started str, optional When it started, in UTC to the millisecond: 2026-10-26T14:00:00.000Z finished str, optional When it finished

The times are text, as the record writes them.

items.title: RecordedInput

What a recipe read through one entry of its output's inputs.

Field Type Meaning entry str The entry, exactly as written content_hash str The hash of what was read size int Its size, in bytes

items.title: Environment

The environment a recipe ran in.

Field Type Meaning iri str An IRI its runner can recreate the environment from

items.title: Runner

The runner that ran a recipe.

Field Type Meaning id str The runner's name version str Its version

  "address": "fit#baseline",
  "content_hash": "sha256:2f52064dbe4ae7fa6932e26efc33bdf8c4e38b9fb958d8e34a08d51e72d0de5a",
  "generated_by": {
    "commit": "b0e28a260c752e8060197b5f788086c53233cb4f",
    "environment": {"iri": "urn:example:python-3.13"},
    "finished": "2026-11-15T10:04:22.950Z",
    "inputs": [
      {
        "content_hash": "sha256:9c6536d38fa37da58fac066342747e6d20fdace12ab5b287cf04506f2afe95b0",
        "entry": "catalog",
        "size": 4
      }
